evidence.quote: And of course, in our Education Packages we get free tokens and we all know what we can do with tokens, right? What can we do with tokens? We can mine the one coin

So in our education packages, what I normally say to people, you pay 5000 euros for a Tycoon package, but you get real value through real education. This opportunity only is now. It means come in, mine your coins, and that's it.

textual.context: The ASR presents the package and token-mining statements in a promotional-sounding first-person sales context. The supplied description uses critical language, but does not establish whether the video creator endorses or merely reports the ASR statements.
textual.potential_relevance: A stated 5,000-euro payment for a package is linked to receiving free tokens and being told to "mine your coins," with an urgency statement that "This opportunity only is now."
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the actual nature, value, availability, or outcome of the tokens or mining, whether payment occurred, or whether the speaker's claims were accurate.

textual.observation: The speaker links learning through the One Academy program with profit and says viewers need to upgrade to the top package to obtain level 5.

evidence.quote: The more you know the more you will profit
The level 5 is in the Tycoon package. So everybody needs to at least upgrade to the top package to get level 5.

textual.context: These statements appear within a presentation describing education packages. The records do not clarify whether the profit statement is a general educational claim, a specific return claim, or how level 5 relates to any financial outcome.
textual.potential_relevance: The source connects a stated profit-oriented message to an education program and conditions access to level 5 on upgrading to the top package.
textual.limitations: No payment amount is stated in the cited upgrade passage, and the records do not establish that an upgrade produces profit, that level 5 has financial value, or that viewers acted on the request.

visual.observation: A presentation slide states that viewers who complete education levels 1 through 5 are expected to upgrade to the top-level "tycoon package" and will receive a certificate after answering all academy questions.
visual.context: Shown in a presentation headed "ONECOIN - THE REAL THING?" and attributed on-screen to "MR GREENWOOD"; the sampled frame does not establish whether this is promotion, quotation, criticism, or documentary discussion.
visual.potential_relevance: The stated upgrade/payment-related condition is linked to completion of educational levels and a promised certificate, creating a specific action-to-benefit relationship that may merit review.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show the package price, payment process, whether anyone acted on the instruction, or whether a certificate was actually issued; the speaker's role and the surrounding context are unclear.

visual.observation: A slide states that an education package is normally described as costing "5000€ for a tycoon package" while providing "REAL EDUCATION"; a subsequent slide states, "This education for 5000€ is worth no more than 10€".
visual.context: These statements appear as part of the same presentation sequence, with the later slide presenting a negative assessment of the stated package value; the sampled frames do not establish whether the statements are an advertisement, a quotation, or commentary.
visual.potential_relevance: The specific €5,000 purchase claim is directly linked to the promised educational benefit, while the following slide supplies an explicit source-side value criticism; together they provide a concrete price-and-benefit relationship for conditional review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish that the package was purchased, that the stated price was current or universally applicable, or that the €10 valuation was independently verified; no transaction outcome or actual loss is visible.

textual_context_notes.observation: The description characterizes the referenced OneAcademy material with critical language.

visual_context_notes.observation: The sampled presentation is visually titled "ONECOIN - THE REAL THING?" and later displays the heading "THE BLACKLIST".

The slides repeatedly identify the segment as "MR GREENWOOD REVEALS FUTURE PLANS FOR THE ONEACADEMY" and include an image of a person beside the text, but the frames do not establish the person's identity or role.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents and criticizes a OneCoin promotional presentation rather than endorsing participation in it. The quoted speaker promotes paid education packages and token mining, while the video frames the claims skeptically, including the visible criticism that the 5000€ education is worth no more than 10€ and the closing label "THE BLACKLIST."
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: N01 fits because the supplied frames and commentary examine and criticize a third-party OneCoin sales presentation. Although the ASR contains promotional claims from the quoted speaker, the video's surrounding framing identifies those claims as questionable rather than recommending that viewers purchase the packages.
